newsitem.title: FINLAND: Helsinki climbs to 11-month high on Wall St gains.
newsitem.headline: Helsinki climbs to 11-month high on Wall St gains.

text.p: Shares ended at a new 11-month high after a moderately active Monday session as Nokia and U.S. stocks advanced in early dealings on Wall Street, extending Friday's gains, brokers said.
The HEX index rose 1.06 percent to 2,152.77, its highest close since Octoaber 2, 1995. Volume was fair at 323 million markka.
But brokers sensed increasing caution on the market as the HEX has already risen some 22 percent this year.
"Many investors prefer to take profits as we are breaking year-highs," one broker said.
Telecoms heavyweight Nokia closed fair trade up 6.50 markka at 196.50. The share accounted for 42 percent of bourse turnover.
Insurer Pohjola's B-share ended lively trade up 1.50 markka at 84.50 after hitting a new calendar year-high 85.00 markka.
Insurer Sampo closed at a two-year high 300.00 markka, up 6.00, after fair volume.
Pharmaceuticals wholesaler Tamro was boosted by healthy January-August sales data released last week, brokers said. It closed 0.80 markka up at 31.50 after hitting a five-year high 32.00 markka.

Forestries tracked other sectors higher, with the sub-index gaining 0.95 percent. But trade was dampened by news that Morgan Stanley had lowered its recommendations for Swedish paper stocks, brokers said.
